title: Maximum Path Sum in a Binary Tree
description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes has an edge connecting them. Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.
input_format: First line contains `n`. Second line contains level-order tokens.
hints: At each node, compute the maximum gain that can be continued up to its parent.
If gain from a subtree is negative, ignore it by using `max(gain, 0)`.
Update global max with `node.val + left_gain + right_gain`.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    tokens = data[1:1+n]
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, v): self.v = int(v); self.left = None; self.right = None
    from collections import deque
    root = Node(tokens[0])
    qu = deque([root])
    idx = 1
    while qu and idx < len(tokens):
        curr = qu.popleft()
        if idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx] != 'null':
            curr.left = Node(tokens[idx]); qu.append(curr.left)
        idx += 1
        if idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx] != 'null':
            curr.right = Node(tokens[idx]); qu.append(curr.right)
        idx += 1
    max_sum = float('-inf')
    def max_gain(node):
        nonlocal max_sum
        if not node: return 0
        left_gain = max(max_gain(node.left), 0)
        right_gain = max(max_gain(node.right), 0)
        price_newpath = node.v + left_gain + right_gain
        max_sum = max(max_sum, price_newpath)
        return node.v + max(left_gain, right_gain)
    max_gain(root)
    print(max_sum)
